name: Ironpass MedCore Emergency Paramedic Full Rig
description: High-visibility signal-orange trauma jacket with retro-reflective chest panels and sealed interior pockets over reinforced black cargo trousers with quick-release tabs at both knees. A hard-shell response helmet in orange with a flip-down polycarbonate visor integrates a BCI vitals relay and radio receiver. Heavy-duty exam gloves in orange nitrile extend past the wrist, and waterproof steel-toe lace-up boots handle flood-slick and debris-strewn terrain. A dual-shoulder harness and rear pack combination carries defibrillator cassettes, trauma foam, airway tools, and a collapsible splint set.
functionality: BCI vitals relay in helmet transmits patient data to hospital intake before arrival; rear pack deploys full trauma kit in a flat layout for roadside or corridor triage.
what_it_says: This person arrives in the worst moment of someone's life and is the single most competent thing in the room.
story_hooks: The BCI relay has been quietly logging GPS coordinates of every call in a district that's been seeing a suspicious uptick in chrome-related injuries.
The trauma foam canister in the rear pack is a replacement unit — the original was used on a patient who was never logged into the system.

physical_description.visual_profile: A high-visibility emergency response uniform commanding immediate recognition. The wearer appears as a mobile trauma station—the signal-orange jacket creates a striking silhouette against urban backgrounds, while the black cargo base grounds the look with tactical authority. The dual-shoulder harness and rear pack add functional bulk that reads as capability rather than clutter.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso to accommodate layered undergarments and equipment access; tapered cargo legs with reinforced knee zones. The harness is adjustable and distributes weight across shoulders and hips. Helmet sits secure with integrated chin strap. Overall cut prioritizes mobility and rapid gear deployment over fashion.
physical_description.primary_material: Signal-orange ballistic nylon jacket with sealed synthetic interior; reinforced black cargo weave trousers; hard-shell polycarbonate helmet; nitrile gloves; waterproof composite boots with steel toe reinforcement
physical_description.texture: Jacket exterior is smooth ballistic weave with retro-reflective raised ridging on chest panels; cargo fabric is slightly textured for grip; helmet is hard-glazed polymer; boots feature rugged tread and weld-seam details
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary signal-orange (jacket, helmet, gloves) with black reinforcement zones and cargo trousers. Retro-reflective silver-white striping across chest and shoulders. Matte black hardware and boot accents.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: heavy-duty friction-fit magnetic snaps with backup velcro flaps. Cargo trousers: friction-lock quick-release tabs at both knees; standard lace closure at waist. Helmet: integrated chin strap with emergency-quick magnetic release. Boots: corrosion-resistant steel laces with elasticated loop-back.
distinctive_features: Retro-reflective chest panels built into jacket exterior for 360° visibility
Integrated BCI vitals relay and radio receiver in helmet crown
Polycarbonate flip-down visor with anti-glare coating
Dual-shoulder harness with quick-access side panels
Rear pack with modular cassette slots for defibrillator units
Sealed interior pockets (waterproof zippers) in jacket
Quick-release knee tabs for rapid trouser removal in contamination scenarios
Ironpass Tactical Medical logo embossed on shoulder patches
Color-coded pocket labels (red for trauma, blue for airway, yellow for splint)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 institutional/municipal. High-quality Ironpass manufacturing signals mid-tier corpo contracts or well-funded emergency services. Not luxury, but clearly superior to salvage-class gear.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by paramedics, emergency response teams, hospital rapid-deployment units, and disaster-zone medical personnel across the GLMZ. The uniform signals immediate authority and medical competence—wearing this outside of active duty is legally restricted in most municipal codes. It reads as 'trained professional' and 'trust me with your life.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in with visible wear patterns—scuffed helmet visor, faded orange on forearms from repeated glove friction, minor staining on cargo legs (cleaned but residual). Equipment pouches show compression marks. Retro-reflective panels remain bright, but jacket fabric may show weathering from repeated decontamination cycles.
